name: Default male crew
description: A deck crew member: MPFB2 (MakeHuman) body on the shared game_engine skeleton (53 bones, Unreal mannequin names), CC0 MakeHuman work suit and shoes, an orange life vest, and five keyed animations. Built by blender/build_crew.py; about 34k triangles.

gender.doc: Body shape. 'male' or 'female' (MPFB gender macro at its end points). Pick a suit and hair to match: male_* suits and short hair for male, female_* suits and bob/long hair for female.

height_cm.doc: Barefoot standing height in centimetres. The builder solves MPFB's height slider until the body measures this within 2 cm; shoes add about 1 cm, hair or a helmet more.

weight.doc: Body mass slider, 0 = very slim, 0.5 = average, 1 = heavy.

muscle.doc: Muscle definition slider, 0 = soft, 0.5 = average, 1 = very muscular.

proportions.doc: MPFB body proportions slider, 0 = unusual, 0.5 = average, 1 = idealised. Optional; defaults to 0.5.

age_years.doc: Age in years. Changes face and body shape, and picks the skin texture age band: young under 40, middle-aged 40-59, old 60 and over.

skin.doc: Skin tone: light, medium or dark. Picks a CC0 MakeHuman skin texture (caucasian, asian or african set) and leans the face shape the same way.

hair.doc: Hair style; omit or null for the default (short02 for male, bob02 for female), "none" for bald.

hair_color.doc: Optional hair (and eyebrow) colour, [r, g, b] each 0..1 in LINEAR values (what a Blender Base Color takes), or null for the style's own dark brown. The texture is recoloured, not tinted, so light colours work: blonde [0.687, 0.479, 0.188], platinum [0.8, 0.75, 0.6], red [0.45, 0.12, 0.04], grey [0.4, 0.4, 0.4], black [0.02, 0.02, 0.02]. The strand pattern is kept.

suit.doc: Outfit (CC0 MakeHuman system assets). male_worksuit01 is blue work overalls over a white T-shirt; casualsuits are jeans/shirts; elegantsuit01 is a business suit. null for none (the body is then visible).

shoes.doc: Footwear. shoes01 brown work shoes (default), shoes02-06 other styles. null for barefoot.

hat.doc: Hat, or null. Only fedoras are in the CC0 pack; for a hard hat use the helmet equipment instead (a hat is dropped when a helmet is worn).

suit_color.doc: Optional tint multiplied over the suit texture, [r, g, b] each 0..1 (e.g. [1, 0.45, 0.1] for orange overalls), or null for the suit's own colours.

shoes_color.doc: Optional tint multiplied over the shoe texture, [r, g, b] each 0..1 (linear), or null. A multiply can only darken: brown shoes tinted white stay brown-ish.

hat_color.doc: Optional tint multiplied over the hat texture, [r, g, b] each 0..1 (linear), or null.

custom_items.doc: Anything the catalog lacks (a singlet, shorts, a held boat hook or torch...). A list of {"id": "item_1", "description": "white singlet", "code": "..."}: Blender Python run after the body and catalog equipment are built and before the animations bake, with bpy, mathutils, math, Vector, Matrix and the helper module crew in scope. No os/sys/subprocess, open, eval, exec. Every object made must be a mesh named Clothes__<Name> (worn) or Equipment__<Name> (held/attached), [A-Za-z0-9_] only. CLOTHES: always use crew.garment(name, regions, color, offset_m=0.008, thickness_m=0.006, z_min=None, z_max=None, trim=0.3, hide_body=True), which cuts the garment from the body's own surface for the bones it covers, so it fits every body and deforms with every animation (never model clothes freehand: they will not move with the body). regions are names from crew.REGIONS: torso, upper_arms, forearms, hands, pelvis, thighs, shins, feet, neck, head (or single bone names like upperarm_l). z_min/z_max are rest-pose hem heights in metres; get them from joints, e.g. hip = crew.joint_z("thigh_l"), knee = crew.joint_z("calf_l"), ankle = crew.joint_z("foot_l"). Recipes: singlet = garment("Clothes__Singlet", ["torso", "pelvis"], c, z_min=hip - 0.03); T-shirt = ["torso", "upper_arms"] with z_min=hip; long sleeves add forearms; shorts = ["pelvis", "thighs"], z_min=(hip + knee) / 2, z_max=hip + 0.12; trousers = ["pelvis", "thighs", "shins"], z_max=hip + 0.12, z_min=ankle + 0.03. A layer worn over another needs a larger offset_m (e.g. 0.014 for shorts over a singlet). Set clothes.suit to null when replacing the outfit, or the suit shows through. HELD ITEMS: build a low-poly mesh with bm = crew.new_bmesh(), crew.box(bm, center, size), crew.cylinder(bm, center, radius, depth, segments, axis), then obj = crew.object_from_bmesh("Equipment__BoatHook", bm, color); model it as if held upright in a relaxed hanging hand: grip at the origin, +Z up, +X forward, sizes in metres; then crew.hold(obj, "right") (or "left"). Worn-but-rigid items (badge, torch on a belt): place at rest-pose coordinates (crew.joint(bone) gives positions; the character faces +X, +Y is its left, +Z up) and crew.attach(obj, bone). crew.material(name, color) makes a plain material. Keep the whole crew under 40000 triangles. A failing item fails the build, naming its id and line.

equipment.doc: Procedural low-poly items, each a mesh Equipment__<name> parented to a bone: life_vest (spine_02, orange by default), helmet (head, white hard hat), binoculars (spine_03, hanging on the chest), radio (pelvis, on the right hip). An entry may also be {"name": "life_vest", "color": "navy"}; colours: orange, navy, yellow, white, red, black, or [r,g,b].

animations.doc: glTF animations, named exactly: idle (3 s breathing and weight-shift loop), walk (1.1 s in-place loop), brace (2.6 s: knees bend, right hand forward-down onto a rail, hold, return), hands_up (2.4 s: raise both hands, hold, lower), squat (2.4 s: down, hold, up). Hand-keyed first drafts; feet stay planted on idle, brace, hands_up and squat.
